note: Each edge here lies on a cycle of requires, which can only shrink. Measured at main 2007b64, 71 edges among 25 blueprints were one strongly connected component; wt/layering took the patterns out (checks/layering.json) and turned the framework edges whose direction was not in doubt. What was left was two questions only the owner could settle. The owner decided the first on 2026-11-05: architecture/admin declares the operator surface, its behaviours, the /v1/admin/* endpoints and token-exchange, and architecture/orchestrator binds it, so admin no longer requires the orchestrator. What is left is whether architecture/storage catalogues every component's stores with their row types bound, or each owner declares its own. An edge is removed when it no longer lies on a cycle; edges are never added.

store catalogue.question: architecture/storage defines which component owns each store and binds its row types (AgentEntry, DomainWorkflow, AgentMetrics, EntityContext; also WorkflowExecution and TaskRecord off the cycle), while those components require storage for its contract. Does storage catalogue its consumers' stores?
options: no: each owner declares its stores in its own Storage section (schemas/common), binding storage's contract; storage keeps the contract (StoreInterface, sealed logs, durable records, snapshots) and drops its requires of orchestrator, domain, gateway and agents/*
yes, untyped: storage keeps the catalogue as prose linking each owner, and drops the requires and bindings
yes, typed: the row types move to protocol/types, which storage and the owners both bind
